questions.question: The ratio of the weight of Ram, Shyam and Mohan is 7 ∶ 8 ∶ 5 respectively. The average weight of Ram, Shyam and Mohan is 80 kg. What is the average weight of Ram and Shyam?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the weights of Ram, Shyam, and Mohan be 7x, 8x, and 5x respectively.

Total weight = 7x + 8x + 5x = 20x.

Since the average weight is 80 kg, total weight = 80 × 3 = 240 kg.

20x = 240 ⇒ x = 12 kg.

Average weight of Ram and Shyam = (7x + 8x) ÷ 2 = 7.5x = 7.5 × 12 = 90 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of weights of Ram, Shyam, and Mohan = 7 : 8 : 5

Average weight of all three persons = 80 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c56b6c337d2f688a829ac1a1eae2ea4ad5c9a367ab4acdea4f4fc43fd79a162b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of Ram, Shyam, and Mohan = Average weight × Number of persons

⇒ Total weight = 80 × 3 = 240 kg

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 7 + 8 + 5 = 20 parts

⇒ Value of 1 part = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 kg

⇒ Weight of Ram = 7 × 12 = 84 kg

⇒ Weight of Shyam = 8 × 12 = 96 kg

⇒ Total weight of Ram and Shyam = 84 + 96 = 180 kg

⇒ Average weight of Ram and Shyam = 180 ÷ 2 = 90 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 90 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Averages

The average provides the central or mean value of a set of quantities. Formula: Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Ratio and Proportion

When a total sum is distributed in a given ratio (a : b : c), the value of any specific share is calculated as: Share = (Ratio part ÷ Sum of all parts) × Total Value.

Weighted Average

Used when combining different groups of different sizes and individual averages into a single overall average. Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: In a 500 m race, P runs at 2 kmph. P gives Q a head start of 20 m and still beats him by 60 seconds. Find the speed of Q.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by P to complete 500 m = 500 ÷ (2 × 5/18) = 900 seconds.

Since P beats Q by 60 s, time taken by Q = 900 + 60 = 960 seconds.

Q gets a 20 m head start, so distance run by Q = 500 − 20 = 480 m.

Speed of Q in m/s = 480 ÷ 960 = 0.5 m/s.

Speed of Q in kmph = 0.5 × (18/5) = 1.8 kmph.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total race distance = 500 m

⇒ Speed of P = 2 kmph

⇒ Head start of Q = 20 m

⇒ P beats Q by = 60 seconds

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Speed in kmph = Speed in m/s × 18/5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51ed1432eadc49c15f6c1e71fdb8e85854497a8113f6370cac39cb8c54c66b4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of P in m/s = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken by P to complete 500 m = 500 ÷ (5/9) = (500 × 9) ÷ 5 = 900 seconds

⇒ Since P beats Q by 60 seconds, time taken by Q to reach the finish line = 900 + 60 = 960 seconds

⇒ Q received a head start of 20 m, so Q covers only 500 − 20 = 480 m

⇒ Speed of Q in m/s = Distance ÷ Time = 480 ÷ 960 = 0.5 m/s

⇒ Converting Q's speed to kmph = 0.5 × (18/5) = 1.8 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Head Start in a Race

If A gives B a head start of x meters in a race of length L, then A must cover L meters, but B only needs to cover (L − x) meters.

Beating by Time

If A beats B by t seconds, it means B arrives t seconds later than A at the finish line. Thus, Time of B = Time of A + t.

Unit Conversion for Speed

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: A batsman scored 96 runs which included 2 boundaries and 6 sixes. What percent of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?
questions.solution:
**Given**

The total score of the batsman: 96 runs

Score from boundaries: 2 x 4 = 8 runs

Score from sixes: 6 x 6 = 36 runs

**Concept Used:** Percentage = (part / total) x 100

**Solution:**

Runs made by running between the wickets = Total score - score from boundaries - score from sixes = 96 - 8 - 36 = 52 runs

Percentage of score made by running = (52 / 96) x 100 = 54.16%

**Therefore, the percentage of his total score that he made by running between the wickets is 54.16%.**

questions.question: Manoj invests Rs.57,695, which is 11% of his annual income, in mutual funds. What is his monthly income? (Rounded up to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
**Given**

Manoj's investment in mutual funds: Rs. 57,695

This investment is 11% of his annual income

**Concept Used: **Calculation of income based on the percentage

**Solution:**

(100/11) × Rs. 57,695 = Rs. X,

where X is his annual income.

X = (100/11) × 57695 ≈ Rs. 524500.

Next, to find out Manoj's monthly income, we divide his annual income by 12.

Therefore, Manoj's monthly income = Rs. 524500/12 ≈ Rs.43,708.33

So, Manoj's monthly income is approximately Rs. 43,708.33.

**Therefore, Manoj's monthly income is approximately Rs. 43,708.33.**

questions.question: If 9 persons can do a job in 18 days, then 18 persons with twice the efficiency can do the same job in:
questions.solution:
**Given**

9 persons can do a job in 18 days

18 persons have twice the efficiency

**Concept Used:**

Work = Number of persons x Efficiency x Time

**Solution:**

Total work = 9 persons x 1 (efficiency) x 18 days = 162 person-days

Time taken by 18 persons with twice the efficiency = Total work / (18 persons x 2 (efficiency)) = 162 person-days / 36 = 9/2 days

**Therefore, 18 persons with twice the efficiency can do the same job in 9/2 days.**

questions.question: A sphere of radius 6 m is cut into two equal halves. Find the volume of each hemisphere so formed. (Use pi=(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
Given:

A sphere of radius 6 m is cut into two equal halves

Formula used:

Volume of sphere = 4/3 π r3 

Calculations:

According to the question,

Volume = 4/3 × π × (6)3 

⇒ Volume = 4 × π × (6)2 × 2

⇒ Volume = 4 × π × 72

⇒ Volume = 288π m3 

Since the sphere is cut in two equal halves then, volume of each sphere = (288π)/2 = 144π m3 

⇒ 144 × 22/7 = 452.57 m³

∴ The volume of each hemisphere so formed is 452.57 m3.

questions.question: The marked price of a toy is Rs.1,600. If the shopkeeper declares a discount of 10% and then 10% cash discount, then what is the selling price of the toy?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The multiplying factor for a 10% discount is 90/100 or 9/10.

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (9/10) × (9/10)

SP = 1600 × (81 / 100)

SP = 16 × 81 = 1296

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1,296.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price of the toy (MP) = Rs.1,600

First discount (D₁) = 10%

Second cash discount (D₂) = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2162bf53db0835071ff55fb13ec996076a472ecfd261f44f7077523b8aa593d6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 1600 − (10% of 1600)

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 1600 − 160 = 1440

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 1440 − (10% of 1440)

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 1440 − 144 = 1296

⇒ Final Selling Price = Rs.1,296

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1,296.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of D₁% and D₂%, the single equivalent discount percentage is D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) / 100.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

All discounts are calculated strictly on the Marked Price (MP), whereas Profit and Loss percentages are based exclusively on the Cost Price (CP).

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which a seller increases the price of goods above the cost price. Markup % = (MP − CP) / CP × 100.
</p

questions.question: The valuation of a house depreciates at the rate of 10% in a year, compared to its value at the beginning of that year. If the current value of the house is ₹40,00,000, then what will be the value of house after three years?
questions.solution:
**Given**

The current value of the house: ₹40,00,000

Depreciation rate: 10% per year

**Concept Used:**

Depreciation = Original cost x (Depreciation Rate/100) x Time

**Solution:**

Value after first year = ₹40,00,000 - (₹40,00,000 x (10/100)) = ₹36,00,000

Value after second year = ₹36,00,000 - (₹36,00,000 x (10/100)) = ₹32,40,000

Value after third year = ₹32,40,000 - (₹32,40,000 x (10/100)) = ₹29,16,000

**Therefore, the value of the house after three years is ₹29,16,000.**

questions.question: Reeta says that she sells her goods at the cost price. If she uses 80 gram weight instead of 100 gram, then what is her profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

The original weight = 80 g

The weight for selling = 100 g

Concept:

P = SP - CP Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

Calculation:

Let the profit % be X

The cost price for the weight = 80 g

The selling price for the weight = 100 g

According to the questions

⇒ X = {100 - 80over 80} times 100 = {20over 80} times 100 = 25\% 

∴ The required result will be 25%

questions.solution:

2nd Proportional q = s2t

3rd Proportional r = st2 

Formula Used:

4th Proportional s=(qr)/(p)

Calculations:

According to the formula,

⇒ 4th Proportional = (s2t × st2)/s3

⇒ 4th Proportional = t³

∴ The fourth proportion is t³.

questions.question: The average weight of 10 persons increases by 7.9 kg when a new person replaces one of them weighing 20 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight increase = Total persons × Average increase

Total increase = 10 × 7.9 = 79 kg

New person's weight = Replaced person's weight + Total increase

New person's weight = 20 + 79 = 99 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 99 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b32c2bcfd844022098093e1275e6d3bf0f2a842bc51559356d090fb979779892.png] 

**Given:**

Number of persons = 10

Weight of replaced person = 20 kg

Increase in average weight = 7.9 kg

**Formula Used:**

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total members × Increase in average)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight increase of the group = 10 × 7.9

⇒ Total increase = 79 kg

⇒ Weight of the new person = 20 + 79

⇒ Weight of the new person = 99 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 99 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement in Averages

When a new item replaces an old item, causing the average to increase, the value of the new item is calculated as: New Value = Old Value + (Total Items × Increase in Average).

Decrease in Average on Replacement

If the replacement causes the average to drop, it means the new item is smaller. The formula is: New Value = Old Value − (Total Items × Decrease in Average).

Addition of a New Member

When a completely new member joins the group (without replacing anyone) and changes the average: New Member's Value = Old Average + (New Total Members × Change in Average).

questions.question: Anand can row 8 km/h in still water. It takes him thrice as long to row up as to row down the stream. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the upstream time is n times the downstream time, the ratio of the boat speed (v) to the stream speed (u) is (n + 1) : (n − 1).

Given boat speed v = 8 km/h and n = 3.

⇒ 8 : u = (3 + 1) : (3 − 1)

⇒ 8 : u = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1

⇒ u = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (v) = 8 km/h

Let the speed of the stream be u km/h.

Let the time taken to row downstream be t hours.

Then, the time taken to row upstream is 3t hours.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Downstream speed = v + u

Upstream speed = v − u

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40758a2d78770f80982ca176997302427578be9b0d94274c298aa073728f24fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed = (8 + u) km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = (8 − u) km/h

⇒ The distance traveled downstream is equal to the distance traveled upstream.

⇒ (8 + u) × t = (8 − u) × 3t

⇒ 8 + u = 3 × (8 − u)

⇒ 8 + u = 24 − 3u

⇒ u + 3u = 24 − 8

⇒ 4u = 16

⇒ u = 4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream & Upstream Speed

Downstream speed (D) = v + u | Upstream speed (U) = v − u

Boat & Stream Speed Calculations

Speed of boat in still water (v) = (D + U) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream (u) = (D − U) ÷ 2

Average Speed for Round Trip

The average speed for a boat to travel a certain distance downstream and return back is given by (v² − u²) ÷ v.
</p

questions.question: On a certain principal, the compound interest, compounded annually, for the second year at 20% per annum is Rs.1,300. The principal is (consider nearest integral value):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The compound interest, compounded annually, for the second year at 20% per annum is Rs.1,300.

**Calculation:**

Since the compound interest obtained for 2nd year is Rs. 1300

That means it is the simple interest on the principal of 2nd year which is (Main principal + Interest of 1st year)

⇒ 1300 = [Principal of 2nd year] × 20/100

⇒ [Principal of 2nd year] = 6500

We know that,

[Principal of 2nd year] = Main principal + Interest of 1st year

Suppose the main principal is P

⇒ P + [P × 20 × 1] /100 = 6500

⇒ 1.2P = 6500

⇒ P = 5416

**∴ Principal amount = Rs. 5416**

questions.question: Two cars start taking laps of a circular track of 3.6 kms at the same time of 12:00 PM. They start from the same point and they are moving in the same direction. Their speeds are 72 kmph and 90 kmph respectively. At what time will the cars meet again?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Circular track length: 3.6 km

Speed of the first car: 72 kmph

Speed of the second car: 90 kmph

**Concept Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Solution:**

The time it takes for two objects moving at different speeds to meet again on a circular track is equal to the time it takes for the faster object to lap the slower one.

The relative speed of the cars is 90 kmph - 72 kmph = 18 kmph.

The time it takes for the faster car to lap the slower car is 3.6 km / 18 kmph = 0.2 hours = 12 minutes.

**Therefore, the cars will meet again at 12:12 PM.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells oil at ₹200 per litre, which he purchased for ₹160 per litre, but he gives only 800 ml of oil instead of 1 litre while selling. Find the actual percentage of profit.
questions.solution:
**Given**

The selling price of oil: ₹200 per litre

Purchase price: ₹160 per litre

Quantity of oil given: 800 ml

**Concept Used:**

Profit percentage = (Selling price - Cost price) / Cost price × 100

**Solution**

Here, the shopkeeper claims to sell the oil at ₹200 per litre, but in reality, he is only providing 800 ml of oil.

Therefore, his effective selling price is actually ₹250 per litre (since ₹200 for 800 ml implies ₹250 for 1000 ml or 1 litre).

So, the profit per litre of oil sold is ₹250 - ₹160 = ₹90.

**Therefore, the profit percentage is (₹90 / ₹160) × 100 = 56.25%.**
